text:
# 你不需要找回原来那批关键词

- 作者：Flavio Amiel（@fba）
- 原帖发布时间：2026-09-19 00:48（北京时间）
- 原帖：https://x.com/fba/status/2100990391990251563
- 收藏日期：2026-10-29
- 英文标题：You don't need the same keywords.

## 中文全文

![Image](<../../90_附件/FBA/HSg3ApbXYAArsB-.jpg>)

我发现了怎样找回流失的 SEO 流量。

但不是你想的那种方式：并不是重新拿回‘同一批’关键词的排名。

你看，过去 4 年成立的许多初创公司，都在经历类似的事情。

它们在最初 12–36 个月里，SEO 增长势头非常好，但后来情况开始恶化。

过程往往是这样：

>> 网站的 SEO 增长势头非常好
>> 加倍投入有效的做法
>> 一切看上去都很美好
>> 然后，Google 算法更新了
>> 流量略有下降
>> 他们慌了，不重新审视策略，只是把原来有效的做法再加码到三倍
>> 流量大幅下跌

好消息是，我见过这种模式，而且知道它是可以逆转的。

因为我也曾通过定制 SEO 策略，帮助几家这样的企业恢复增长。

我马上就会告诉你应该怎么做。

下面是一个各项表现都开始恢复的案例：

![Image](<../../90_附件/FBA/HSgzeweWcAA7Xrx.jpg>)

一家正从上述模式中恢复的企业的数据图。

## 把自己埋进坑里的网站

AI 企业刚起步时，它们发布的那些内容，往往还没有多少人在做：

- ‘AI 生成器’的各种变体，就是先发优势的一个好例子。

它们能排上名，是因为其他地方还没有这些词对应的内容。

这些网站：

- 保持着增长势头
- 建立了 SEO 运营流程和文档
- 以及／或者把工作流程交给某个人或 SEO 机构，继续加倍投入

12–48 个月后，模仿者都研究了它们的网站，然后开始做同样的事。

有时对方做得更好、规模更大，或者拥有更高的权威。

还有一类网站，把自己埋进了海量内容，包括 AI 垃圾内容之中。

不少网站拼命推送这些 AI 垃圾内容。

它们试图覆盖尽可能多的信息型查询，争取排名。

但随着时间推移，越来越少的人会去 Google 搜这些问题，因为他们改用 ChatGPT 了。

这两种情况的流量曲线，看起来几乎一样：

- 内容不相关，而且搜索的人越来越少
- 内容仍然相关，但竞争越来越激烈

![Image](<../../90_附件/FBA/HSgzp5DWkAAXTSA.jpg>)

好消息是，这不一定意味着你月度经常性收入（MRR）达到 100 万美元的梦想就此结束。

你可以扭转局面，但需要耐心和努力。

你需要经历以下几个步骤：

- 彻底清理
- 调整内容结构
- 重新研究市场
- 构建适合获得 AI／LLM 提及的内容结构

下面展开讲。

## 彻底清理！

如果你不熟悉 SEO 审计，我建议找一位优秀的 SEO 顾问做一次，因为清理方式会因你的具体情况而不同。

举个例子：

查看 Google Search Console 和 GA4，或者 PostHog 等工具，再根据每个 URL 带来的成果分类：

- 点击
- 转化
- 外链

⚠️ 两个例子

我不会把所有情况都讲完，那足够写成一本书。我这里只举两个例子。

有排名，却没有收益。

页面的展示量很高，但点击率（CTR）很差吗？

如果某个问题的答案如今已经直接显示在搜索结果页上，即使你的页面排在第一页，页面本身也不一定出了问题，重写也救不了它。

你要么把它改造成面向真正会带来点击的查询的页面，要么让它成为辅助材料，链接到需要支持的页面。

完全没有排名。

如果页面还在，也已经被收录，却没有任何作用，那么它就是适合合并和删除的候选对象。

## 内容结构

页面内容有道理，却没有排名。

我可以给你举几百个例子，但真正重要的一点是：

如果你从来没有规划过内容结构，就围绕主题图谱，采用正确的中心与辐射结构（Hub N' Spoke）来搭建。为你的业务核心主题建立长期有效的主页面，让网站获得主题权威的认可。

我做过很多次，每次都有效。这里有一个[最近的博客线框图示例](https://preview.kit-mail3.com/click/dpheh0hzhmh4/aHR0cHM6Ly9odG1sZHJvcHMuY29tL3AvZ3R5d2M3ZG0=)，你可以拿来参考。

## 重新研究市场

你的用户今天在搜什么，明天又会搜什么？

如果你有一款 LinkedIn AI 工具，却仍然在围绕‘AI LinkedIn 聊天机器人’制作内容，那你已经落后了。

你应该改进产品，开始补充如何把 Claude 与 LinkedIn 连接起来的内容，并把你的 MCP 作为解决方案，让产品脱颖而出。

## 适合获得 AI／LLM 提及的内容结构

我们都希望出现在 ChatGPT 等工具的回答中。

但除了那些可能存在的站外技巧，现实是：你需要先把自己网站上的问题解决好。

怎么做？你需要改变现有内容的结构。

具体改什么？首先，对品牌的描述用词要保持一致；然后做好那些常见的细节：没有废话，直接回答明确的问题，让相关实体共同出现，等等。

## 其他一些有效的做法

外链和提及。你永远不应该停止寻找外链机会。我最近最喜欢的方法，是创建以引用中心为核心的页面，让它们自动获得外链。[看看我的另一篇文章《如何免费获得外链》](https://x.com/fba/status/2098503799044243554)。

索引控制。处理分类归档页和分页时，要关注 `index`、`noindex`、`follow`、`nofollow`、指向自身的 canonical、在 `robots.txt` 中禁止抓取等设置。

死路。对于仍被正常页面链接的 404 页面，把它们重定向到最接近的有效 URL，或者主页。指向失效 URL 的内链也要同样处理。别把爬虫引向死胡同。

身份。作者署名有助于 E-E-A-T。把署名放到每篇文章顶部，不要只让它待在文章底部的作者框里。建立真实、完整的作者页面。确保 `BlogPosting` 结构化数据包含 `author.url`，而且指向实际的作者页面，而非 `/about`；否则，实体之间的关联会在你不知情的情况下失效。

分类与内链。把分类页重建为真正的教程中心，而不是缺乏上下文的归档列表。在博客不同页面之间添加有语境的链接。检查免费工具页是否有入链；如果没有，就为值得重点推广的工具建立 10–20 条。

AI 信号。确保你发布的 `robots.txt` 没有自相矛盾。很多人用了 Cloudflare，也启用了它的 AI 功能，却并不真正了解这些设置。我多次见到这样的情况：`Content-Signal` 指令声明 `ai-train=yes`，但同一个文件却明确禁止了 `GPTBot`、`Google-Extended` 和 `ClaudeBot`。

## 不该做什么

指望靠增加发布量走出困境。

流量跌了，本能反应就是多发文章。但这样只会继续增加那些导致你被降权的内容，而且现在你还在以更快的速度做这件事。

把所有内容都重写一遍。

如果你的内容明显是 ChatGPT 3 生成的 AI 垃圾，那当然应该重写。但如果不是，而且你已经有一套像样的质量评估流程，就先别重写。先重组结构，再评估结果，然后根据结果决定重写什么。

这些都不是什么全新的 SEO，所以你可以继续做好以下几件事：

- 发布值得长期保留的页面。
- 成为别人引用的信息来源。
- 回答人们仍会向 Google 提出的问题。

回头聊，

Flavio

---

## 英文原文

I discovered how to get lost SEO traffic back.

But not in the way you think: not by recovering the "same" keywords.

You see, many Startups founded in the past 4 years are going through the same.

They had amazing SEO momentum in the first 12-36 months but things have turned around for the worse.

It goes like this:

>> Website has amazing SEO momentum
>> Doubles down on what’s working
>> Everything is amazing 
>> Then comes an Google’s Algo update
>> Traffic drops a little
>> They freak out and triple down on what working without revising stratetgy
>> Traffic drops massively

The good news is that I’ve seen this pattern and I know it's reversible.

(because I’ve also helped a few of these businesses recover with custom SEO strategies)

And I'll share what to do in a sec.

Example recovery across the board:

![Image](<../../90_附件/FBA/HSgzeweWcAA7Xrx.jpg>)

graph from a business that is recovering from one such pattern

## Sites that buried themselves

When AI businesses got started, they were some of the first publishing what they were publishing:

- "ai generator" variations is a good example of the first-mover advantage

They were ranking because the terms didn't exist somewhere else.

These websites:

- kept the momentum
- stablished SEO Operations and documentation
- and/or handed their workflow to a person or SEO agency to double down

After 12-48 months, every copycat checked their website and started doing the same.

Sometimes better, or at a bigger scale or with more authority.

Then there were the sites that buried themselves in content (and AI Slop).

Many pushed their AI Slop content super hard.

They tried ranking for as many informational queries as they could.

Queries that over time less people are asking Google about (bc they were using ChatGPT instead).

The graph looks almost the same for both cases:

- irrelevant content and less people searching
- relevant content and more competition

![Image](<../../90_附件/FBA/HSgzp5DWkAAXTSA.jpg>)

Now, the good news is that this needn't be the end of your million dollar MRR dream.

You can turn it around, but you need patience and effort.

The steps you're going to go through:

- The Big Clean Up
- Content Structure
- New Market Research
- AI / LLM Mention structure

Let's dig up:

## The Big Clean up!

If you're unfamiliar with SEO audits, I recommend you get one from a good SEO consultant, because these clean ups are going to vary depending on your individual case.

Example:

Check Google Search Console and GA4 (or Posthog, etc.) and Classify every URL by what it earns:

- Clicks
- Conversions
- Backlinks

⚠️Two Examples

I won't cover all the cases because that's a full book, but will give two examples instead:

Ranking but not earning.

Does it have high impressions but terrible CTR?

If it ranks page one on a question the SERP now answers itself, the page isn't broken and rewriting it won't save it.

Either it gets repurposed toward a query with a real click, or it becomes supporting material that links into a page that needs help.

Not ranking at all.

If it exists, it's indexed and it does nothing, then that's a good merge and delete candidate.

## Content Structure

Pages make sense but don't rank.

I can give you hundreds of examples, but the one that REALLY matters is:

if you've never planned your content structure, build it around a Topical Map with the right content structure (Hub N' Spoke) so you can be validated as the authority, by having evergreen main pages that hold the main topics that your business is about.

I've done this so many times, and it works without fail. Here's [an example of a recent wireframe](https://preview.kit-mail3.com/click/dpheh0hzhmh4/aHR0cHM6Ly9odG1sZHJvcHMuY29tL3AvZ3R5d2M3ZG0=) for a blog, so that you can use it as a reference.

## New Market Research

What are your users searching for TODAY and what will they search for TOMORROW?

If you had a LinkedIn AI Tool and you kept doing content about "AI LinkedIn Chatbot" you're behind.

You should improve your product and start adding how to connect Claude with LinkedIn and put your MCP as the solution to make things stand out.

## AI / LLM Mention structure

We all want to show up on ChatGPT, etc.

And besides all the external hacks possible, the reality is you need to fix it first in your own website.

How? You need to change the structure of your current content.

What kind of changes? Well, consistent wording for your brand and the usual suspects at a detail level: no fluff, straight answers to direct questions, entity co-ocurrences, etc.

## Some other stuff that work

Backlinks and mentions. You should never stop looking for backlink opportunities. My favorite way of doing this these days, is to create Citation-hub led pages that collect backlinks on autopilot. ([Check my other article HOW TO GET FREE BACKLINKS](https://x.com/fba/status/2098503799044243554))

Index control. Category archives and pagination where you focus on index,noindex,follow,nofollow, self-referencing canonicals, disallowing in robots.txt, etc.

Dead ends. 404s that were still being linked from live pages, either redirect to the closest live URL or your homepage. Same for internal links pointing at dead URLs. Don't send crawlers into walls.

Identity. The byline authors help with the EEAT. Move them to the top of each article instead of only living in a box at the foot. Have real author pages built out. Make sure the BlogPosting schema had author.url but isn't pointing at /about instead of the actual author page, which quietly breaks the entity link.

Categories and Internal linking. Have your category pages rebuilt as real tutorial hubs instead of archives without context. Add contextual links across the blog. Check that your free tool pages have inbound links, and if they don't, built some 10 to 20 to the tools worth pushing.

AI signals. Make sure you're not publishing a contradicting robots.txt — Many of you use Cloudflare and turn on their AI stuff without really knowing, but I've seen this many times: a Content-Signal directive declared ai-train=yes while the same file explicitly disallowed GPTBot, Google-Extended and ClaudeBot.

## What NOT to do

Publishing your way out.

Traffic's down, so the instinct is more posts: but you'll be adding more of the exact thing that got you demoted, and now you're doing it faster.

Rewriting everything.

If your content is clearly AI slop from ChatGPT 3, then by all means do rewrite it. But if it isn't, and you had a decent quality assessment process, then don't rewrite. Restructure first, then assess results. Then rewrite based on results.

None of this is new SEO, so here's what you can keep doing:

- Publish pages worth keeping.
- Be the source other people cite.
- Answer questions people still ask Google.

Speak soon,

Flavio
